editorial.headline: Music Publishing: Nationally Open, Barred to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Music publishing is nationally open to PMA with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium means a PMA entity cannot register this activity there today.
editorial.body:
Nationally, this activity is open to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Yet the immediate Bali answer is firmer: a PMA business cannot register this activity there today. The difference is not a matter of how a business frames its catalogue or distributes music; it follows the Bali entry attached to the activity, whose stated risk position brings it within the province-wide moratorium. A sound decision has to hold both facts at once: national openness exists, but Bali PMA registration is blocked.

At its core, the activity concerns the publishing life of a musical composition. It covers obtaining and registering copyright for musical compositions, then promoting, licensing and enabling their use. The permitted uses expressly extend across recordings, radio, television, film, live performance, print, podcasts and other media. The scope also includes cooperation in publishing and distributing sound recordings, whether the route is through wholesalers, retailers, direct supply to the public, streaming platforms or digital downloads. Music books and sheet-music books are included as well. It is an activity built around the circulation of musical works and related published material across both traditional and digital channels.

The record makes the activity available at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That range accommodates businesses that publish compositions, manage their use, collaborate on sound-recording publication and distribution, or publish music and score books. It does not reserve the activity for one distribution model: circulation may be physical, direct to the public, streamed or downloaded, provided it remains within the publishing and distribution work described here. For a prospective registrant, the central issue is whether the business is carrying out that rights, publishing, licensing, use and distribution work.

The Bali restriction turns on the record’s stated OSS risk outcome: at the Besar scale, every scope is Low or Medium-Low risk. Bali’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island on a permanent basis. The reason recorded for this activity therefore places it inside that moratorium, dated May 2026. The national 100% ceiling remains the national foreign-ownership position; it does not override the Bali PMA registration block. The practical conclusion is straightforward: foreign investment may be nationally open for this activity, but a PMA entity cannot register it in Bali today.
